subject: Re: Response to your request (our reference 260803049 - SAR)
body_text:
Disclosure Team,

I request an internal review of the SAR response (MoJ reference 260803049)
dated 3 September 2026.

There's 133 houses about to be developed on this land and I am trying to
raise the concern that their title is defective. Please cooperate.

The response states:

“the MOJ does not hold any personal data within the scope of your request.
This is because the files have been destroyed in accordance with the record
retention and disposition schedule (RRDS).”

This conclusion is not adequately supported by the information provided. I
ask the reviewer to address the specific points below.
1. Evidence that the records existed

I hold contemporaneous records from the European Commission of Human Rights
concerning Application No. 14464/88, Buckler v United Kingdom. Those
records establish that a substantial documentary record existed relating to
the underlying proceedings and the United Kingdom Government's handling of
the case.

The existence of that independent documentary trail is directly relevant to
the searches that should have been conducted and to the subsequent fate of
the corresponding Government records.

I therefore ask the reviewer to distinguish between:

   1. records which never existed;
   2. records which existed but were subsequently transferred to another
   department, public authority or archive;
   3. records which existed but were destroyed; and
   4. records which still exist but could not be located by the searches
   undertaken for this SAR.

Your response appears to rely upon category 3, but does not identify the
documentary evidence supporting that conclusion.
2. Searches actually undertaken

Please establish, insofar as recorded information is available:

   - the file references or index references searched;
   - the names and variations searched, including Buckler, Williams,
   Frederick Buckler, Mary Williams/Mrs Buckler and Sion Buckler/Hywel Buckler;
   - the relevant court case numbers or archival references searched;
   - whether historical HM Courts & Tribunals Service and predecessor-body
   records were searched;
   - whether records relating to the 1955 possession proceedings were
   searched;
   - whether records relating to the 1962 Cardiff County Court proceedings
   were searched;
   - whether records relating to the 1974 proceedings, including the
   enforcement proceedings, were searched;
   - whether records relating to the 1986 High Court judgment and 1987
   Court of Appeal proceedings were searched;
   - whether records relating to the Treasury Solicitor/Government Legal
   Department's involvement in the litigation were searched;
   - whether records relating to European Commission of Human Rights
   Application No. 14464/88 were searched;
   - whether records relating to the 1988 enforcement/eviction were
   searched; and
   - whether any records concerning the attendance, identification, welfare
   or safeguarding of children present during the 1988 enforcement were
   searched.

My request was not limited to the original court files. It sought any
personal data relating to me, including as a child present at the 1988
enforcement, contained in any records connected with the specified
proceedings or the Government's handling of Application No. 14464/88.
3. Evidence of destruction or transfer

Your response specifically states that “the files have been destroyed in
accordance with the record retention and disposition schedule (RRDS).”

Please therefore identify:

   - the specific RRDS disposal class or rule relied upon;
   - the version and date of the RRDS applicable to those records;
   - the applicable retention period;
   - the date, or approximate date, on which the relevant records were
   destroyed;
   - whether a destruction certificate, disposal schedule, destruction log
   or equivalent audit record exists;
   - whether the records were destroyed in whole or in part;
   - whether any records were transferred to another department, public
   authority or archive;
   - whether any transfer record exists; and
   - whether any surviving index, catalogue, register, file list, metadata
   or other residual record identifies the files which were destroyed.

Most importantly, please confirm whether the statement that the files “have
been destroyed” is based on an actual surviving disposal record, or is an
inference drawn from the absence of the files in current MoJ/HMCTS holdings.

There is a material difference between those two propositions.

If there is a recorded destruction decision or disposal record, I ask that
the reviewer identify the record and the authority under which the
destruction took place, subject of course to any applicable exemption or
restriction on disclosure.
4. European Commission of Human Rights records

I also ask the reviewer specifically to consider the records associated
with Application No. 14464/88.

I possess records from the European Commission of Human Rights relating to
that application. They provide an independent documentary trail concerning
the underlying dispute and the United Kingdom Government's involvement.

Please therefore clarify whether the MoJ/HMCTS searches included records
concerning Government correspondence, legal submissions, memoranda or other
material relating to that application, including material involving the
Treasury Solicitor or other Government departments.

If such records were historically held by the MoJ or its predecessors but
subsequently transferred elsewhere, please identify the receiving
institution and any known archival or file reference.
5. Conclusion

I am not asking the MoJ to recreate records that no longer exist.

I am asking for an accurate account of what records were held, what
searches were undertaken, what became of those records (destruction or
transfer), and what documentary evidence exists of their disposal.

If, following review, the conclusion remains that no personal data is held,
please provide the reasons for that conclusion together with the recorded
information requested above concerning the historical files and their
disposal.

Please treat this correspondence as a formal request for internal review of
the SAR response.

Regards,


Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
